O.outcome_detail: post-training left inferior frontal gyrus activation during syntactic processing

cells.quote: Yusa and colleagues92 used direct social interaction to compare post-training brain activity in participants who learned Japanese sign language syntax with a native deaf signer to that of those who viewed instructive videos (Fig. 1D). Both groups learned through physically signing, as opposed to passively viewing the teacher or videos. These two conditions directly tested the effect of embodiment, as induced by participants in the live exposure group being physically present with the teacher, and multi-modal social cues, on learning. Syntactic processing post-training led to activations in the left inferior frontal gyrus, similar to that displayed by native listeners in the live exposure group but not in the video viewing group.
cells.note: This is a finding from a reviewed fMRI study; the review does not state assignment procedures, training duration, learner expertise, or a printed effect size.
